hypotheses.H-OP1: WM-S online improves end-to-end success over the strongest learned non-world-model reference (C1)
hypotheses.H-OP1-causal: the training-learned library model (C2a) and library knowledge at all (C2b) are causally necessary
hypotheses.H-OP1-nonlearned: the gain exceeds the strongest non-learned shortcut at the same run budget (C3)
hypotheses.H-OP1-noregression: WM-S is not worse than the reference on any slice (N_*)
hypotheses.H-OP2: WM-S beats the black-box neural world model (C5)
hypotheses.H-OP3: online adaptation of the library model improves over the frozen model (C4)
hypotheses.success_rule: WORLD_MODEL_SUCCESS (this phase, scoped claim) requires C1, C2a, C2b, C3 and every N_* to PROMOTE with agreeing implementations, attack results that do not explain the gain, and independent review; C4 and C5 scope the claim
hypotheses.claim_scope: an exact interpreter of visible Python plus a learned tabular model of an opaque library, used by a verified depth-2 planner, versus learned model-free and non-learned agents with the same two real runs
